pillar_reactions.evidence: Interrupted the pillar to vet the coach's credentials — 'what was this thing, like, he got into kettlebells? Like, how was he trained? Like, not that, to say that he needs, like, a certificate to do this type of stuff, but, like, what's his background in a sense?' — then checked the mechanics of the mobility prescription ('But you can do it in the morning as well, obviously, right?') and recapped the pillar back to the rep unprompted.

Ran ahead of the pitch on his own protocol: 'I've done 96' hour fasts, quarterly 72-96 hour water fasts, planning a five-day with bone broth and electrolytes, already eats close to how Trevor eats — 'I do that too, but yeah. I mean, it's good for your brain, man, eating like that.' Volunteered that he naturally fasts and gets lean in summer at 20,000 steps a day.

Pushed back on the substance of the pillar rather than asking how it works: 'Realistically, though, is it actually him or he has, like, people just answering?... I just want to know if it's actually him. Like, if I message the guy, he's actually doing one-on-one coaching or whatnot.' Backed it with 'I have a few friends that do coaching, fitness coaching. They use AI, the supplement.' Accepted the WhatsApp answer and moved on.

anchors.raw: when I do pavers and stuff, when I pressure wash, some jobs are like either like 2,000 and they go up to 15,000 and then some people get blown away. So that's what it takes.
anchors.note: He sells high-ticket services himself and identifies with the seller's position, so 6,000 read as a normal transaction rather than a shock. This is the strongest supporting anchor in the batch and it is why no OC play was needed.

anchors.raw: I've had a trainer before for weight training, but, like, there's certain things that I've learned from that because, well, I invested the money from his experience
anchors.note: Established precedent of paying for coaching and of valuing what it returned — the opposite of the Nick Hartas call the same day, where there was no coaching spend history at all.

anchors.raw: just recently, just to get myself kind of in the groove, based on looking at Trevor's Instagram post or Facebook post, he puts like some of those workouts in. And so I did them
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free social content, plus ChatGPT and YouTube research
anchors.note: He was already getting a result from the free version, and had done real research with AI tools — 'if you know how to use it well, ask the right questions and prompt it correctly, you could get really good answers, which I have.' The rep pre-empted this cleanly by asking why a coach rather than the internet, which is the reason it never became an objection.

anchors.raw: the other one is, what's his name, Max or something, Max Amelia, I can't remember his name, but anyways, he's from Europe, and then there's one other guy that's from the States... they all look pretty knowledgeable when it comes to it
anchors.competitor: Other prominent online kettlebell coaches, one European and one US-based
anchors.note: He explicitly sees Trevor as one of three interchangeable-looking authorities and said their descriptions of kettlebells are 'very similar'. No differentiation was offered beyond Trevor's personal story; the deal was won on service format, not on coach superiority.

anchors.raw: We have a school program if you want, you know?
anchors.note: Rep-introduced rather than prospect-held, and used deftly to define what this prospect was not buying. Worth tracking: the cheaper in-house product was named without a price at the moment before the 6,000 was quoted.

unmet_demand.want: To buy it through his company and treat it as a business expense — 'I'm thinking if I can do this through my company, running through a company as a, I don't know if, I'm not sure if we're allowed here in Canada to do a write-off, anything related to fitness, but I'll figure out a way.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep did not answer — he deflected into a joke about Canadian rules and the conversation moved to the prospect's exit plans. No invoicing, business-entity billing or receipt question was addressed, and the prospect was left to 'figure out a way' himself.

unmet_demand.want: A 0%-interest instalment route — the prospect named Split It specifically as allowing 12 monthly payments on a credit card at 0%, against Klarna which carries interest
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Only Klarna (with interest), plain credit card, and an in-house split into two or three were offered. Whether a longer 0% route exists was never established on the call.
